article_title: TypeScript 7.0 Ships as General Availability, With Microsoft Citing 8x to 12x Faster Builds From Its Native Go Compiler

content_preview.title: TypeScript 7.0 Ships as General Availability, With Microsoft Citing 8x to 12x Faster Builds From Its Native Go Compiler
content_preview.summary: Microsoft shipped TypeScript 7.0 as generally available on July 8, 2026, moving the compiler and language service to a native Go port that Microsoft says is typically 8x to 12x faster on full builds.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft shipped TypeScript 7.0 as generally available on July 8, 2026, according to the [TypeScript team's announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/), which opens: "Today we are proud to announce the availability of TypeScript 7, a 10x faster native port of TypeScript!" The release replaces the compiler and language service — previously written in TypeScript itself and run on the V8 JavaScript engine — with a full native port written in Go,...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 939 words, within the 400-1200 word News range. Dense with specific, verifiable numbers but each one is explicitly attributed to a named source and reads cleanly rather than as a stat-dump.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots read from local gzip archives at sources/2026-07/typescript-70-ships-as-general-availability-with-microsoft-citing-8x-to-12x-faster-builds-from-its-native-go-compiler/ (source-0.html.gz through source-3.html.gz). Decompressed sha256 of each snapshot matches manifest.json exactly (verified via `gunzip -c | shasum -a 256`), confirming no tampering. source-0 (devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/, GA announcement dated July 8th, 2026 by Daniel Rosenwasser): confirmed opening quote 'Today we are proud to announce the availability of TypeScript 7, a 10x faster native port of TypeScript!'; confirmed '8x and 12x' speedup range verbatim; confirmed all four cited benchmark pairs exactly (VS Code 125.7s->10.6s/11.9x, Sentry 139.8s->15.7s/8.9x, Bluesky 24.3s->2.8s/8.7x, Playwright 12.8s->1.47s/8.7x) against the default --checkers 4 table (article correctly uses the default-config numbers, not the --checkers 8 alternate table also present on the page); confirmed memory deltas (VS Code 5.2GB->4.2GB/-18%, within the cited 6%-26% range across the four benchmarked projects); confirmed editor responsiveness quote (17.5s -> under 1.3s, 'over 13x faster') verbatim; confirmed '80% fewer' failing language server commands and '60% less' crashes; confirmed company list (Slack, Vanta, Canva, Figma, Google, Bloomberg, Linear, Notion) all appear among the named testers; confirmed Slack quote (40% merge queue reduction, CI 7.5min->1.25min) verbatim; confirmed Vanta 'up to 9x' and Canva '58 seconds...to about 4.8 seconds' verbatim; confirmed Microsoft News Services '400 hours a month' verbatim; confirmed npm/@typescript/native-preview (8.5 million weekly downloads) and typescript@next migration; confirmed @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package and tsc6 executable; confirmed --checkers (default 4)/--builders/--singleThreaded flags; confirmed locked defaults (strict, module: esnext, noUncheckedSideEffectImports, stableTypeOrdering) and types defaulting to []; confirmed removed options (target: es5, downlevelIteration, moduleResolution node/node10, amd/umd/systemjs/none); confirmed the Vue/MDX/Astro/Svelte/Angular non-support caveat verbatim. source-1 (announcing-typescript-7-0-rc, dated June 18th, 2026, byline Daniel Rosenwasser, Principal Product Manager): confirms RC date and author exactly as cited. source-2 (theregister.com, July 9, 2026 byline): confirmed opening line 'The Microsoft-led TypeScript 7.0 features an order-of-magnitude speed boost...' verbatim; confirmed independent reproduction of the 8x-12x quote attributed to Rosenwasser; confirmed 'With TypeScript 7, full type checks can be done by the developer again at Slack' verbatim; confirmed both Hejlsberg quotes ('lowest level language we can get to...' and 'We quickly realized we could get 10x, half of it from being native code...') verbatim and correctly attributed (one from a Microsoft video, one an earlier remark, exactly as the article frames them); confirmed Steve Lucco co-creation credit. source-3 (github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/releases): confirmed tag typescript/v7.0.2, timestamp '08 Jul 15:58' (datetime attribute 2026-07-08T15:58:56Z), and a direct link back to the devblogs GA announcement — corroborating the ship date exactly as the article states. No hallucinated quotes, no misattributed specifics, no orphan claims found across any of the four sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, quote, and named entity in the body traces to one of the four cited sources with verbatim or near-verbatim accuracy. The 'just under three weeks after the RC' framing (June 18 -> July 8 = 20 days) is arithmetically correct. The internal cross-reference to the May 2026 TypeScript 7.0 Beta article (/article/2026-05/15-microsoft-releases-typescript-70-beta-with-go-based-native-compiler-for-up-to-10x-faster-builds) resolves to an existing published article. No fabrications detected.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Claims attributed to Microsoft are consistently marked as Microsoft's own framing ('Microsoft says', 'according to the announcement') rather than presented as independent verification, which is appropriate given all performance figures originate from the vendor's own benchmarks. The Analysis section stays descriptive rather than promotional.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers the TypeScript 7.0 GA release; checked all of src/content/articles/2026-07/ for duplicates. This is a natural follow-up to the existing Beta (2026-05) and 6.0 (2026-03/2026-04) coverage, not a rewrite of it.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Exceptionally well-sourced submission — every one of roughly 25 discrete factual claims (benchmarks, quotes, dates, config changes) was independently verified against the four source snapshots and matched exactly, with correct attribution throughout. No corrections needed. APPROVE.
